thread:
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT: ingress-eu 5xx spike detected (alert: ingress.errors_rate > 5% for 3m). Paging on-call.
Maya (on-call): seeing the alert, joining. ETA 2m to check dashboards :eyes:
Maya (on-call): quick check — errors are concentrated on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 -> upstream service timeouts. Traffic spike from region-eu-batch jobs?
Jonah R.: I'm available, switching into incident. Maya, want me to take over? I'm closer to the routing playbooks.
Maya (on-call): yes please. handing over. current mitigation: scaled deployment ingress-eu +2 replicas, disabled sticky-session for that route, but errors persist.
Jonah R.: noted. checking LB logs.
Jonah R.: LB shows 502/504 from ASG targets, unhealthy targets in eu-west-1 pool.
Priya: flagging customer-impact — we have three enterprise customers in EU seeing elevated errors (support tickets inbound). Prioritize mitigation and notify CS.
Maya (on-call): pinging @cs-team: heads up, enterprise customers in EU have elevated errors. Please prepare shielded comms.
SRE-Bot: Incident channel created: #inc-1739998888-ingress-eu
Evan: I can start regional failover to eu -> us-west for non-data-residency routes. But need approval from on-call.
Jonah R.: do it. Route only non-sensitive traffic. Run gradual shift 10% -> 50% -> 100% if stable.
Liu: adding that some pods are OOM-killed, crashloops on one node in eu-west-1; might be a bad hot-path in the new quantization branch.
Nadia: I can rollback the quantization feature flag in eu cluster. Do we want to try rollback or failover first?
Jonah R.: failover first to reduce customer impact while we assess root cause. Nadia, prepare rollback as T+10 if errors persist after failover.
Maya (on-call): executing failover plan: running canary shift to us-west.
Maya (on-call): command:
```\n# shift 10% traffic to us-west
POST /admin/routing/shift HTTP/1.1
Host: router-api.internal
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "from_region":"eu-west-1",
  "to_region":"us-west-2",
  "percent":10,
  "routes":["/v1/generate"]
}
```
Jonah R.: watch metrics: error_rate, p95 latency, backend 5xx. If error spike continues in us-west, rollback immediately.
SRE-Bot: Alert: failover shift step applied (10%).
Maya (on-call): 10% moved, error rate dropped for EU customers reporting — still elevated but trending down. Tickets updated.
Priya: CS update: customers A/B reported reduced errors after shift. Good signal.
Liu: digging into pod logs. Found stack traces referencing new encoder optimization: NullPointer in kv-cache path. Crash reason matches OOM traces.
Nadia: starting rollback of feature flag in eu cluster now.
Nadia: command:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/ingress-eu QUANT_OPT=false
kubectl rollout status deploy/ingress-eu
```
Nadia: rollout succeeded, pods stable, crashloops stopped.
Jonah R.: good. scale down old temp replicas and revert traffic incrementally to eu-west.
Maya (on-call): shifting back 50% -> 100% after verifying 5m stable window.
SRE-Bot: note: increased alert noise during failover — many transient 500s triggered dedup suppression
Evan: post-incident, we need to tune alerting to avoid paging on short failovers. Proposal:
- Increase ingress.errors_rate alert from 5% over 3m to 7% over 5m for EU region-only alerting.
- Add a composite alert that requires both errors_rate > threshold AND backend target unhealthy_count > 3.
- Implement short-term suppression during automated failover windows (60s) to avoid duplicate pages.
Jonah R.: agree with composite alert. Right now we page on noisy 1-min spikes. Make it 5m and include backend health to reduce false positives.
Maya (on-call): also add a dashboard panel that shows routing shift percentages and failover events correlated with 5xx spikes — will help postmortem.
Liu: will add a grafana panel: "Regional Failover -> Error Correlation" showing time series: ingress.errors_rate, routing.shift_percent, backend_unhealthy_count.
Priya: CS asks for timeline and impact numbers. Can we export per-customer error rates during window?
Jonah R.: yes. run quick query:
```
SELECT customer_id, count(*) as errors
FROM logs.production
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2024-08-20T15:02:00Z' AND '2024-08-20T15:25:00Z'
AND path='/v1/generate' AND status >= 500
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Maya (on-call): results attached to incident doc. Top 3 customers accounted for 62% of errors.
Nadia: creating an incident follow-up checklist:
- [x] Failover executed and reversed
- [x] Feature rollback applied in eu
- [x] Customer comms drafted (Priya)
- [ ] Alert tuning PR (Jonah)
- [ ] Dashboard panels (Liu)
- [ ] Postmortem doc (Maya)
Jonah R.: I'll open an Alerting PR: change conditions + add composite rule + add suppression window for automated failovers. ETA EOD.
Liu: I'll add dashboard panels and a Grafana alert that mirrors the composite rule for visual confirmation.
Priya: I'll coordinate customer emails and include mitigation timeline; will cc security for any compliance concerns.
Maya (on-call): any lingering issues? I'm seeing error rate back to normal for 20m. Marking incident as mitigated. Moving to post-incident.
SRE-Bot: Incident #1739998888 status: MITIGATED -> Monitoring.
Jonah R.: action items assigned. I'll link PRs in the incident doc and schedule brief review tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
Maya (on-call): handing off to next on-call (Jonah) for postmortem runbook. Good job team :thumbsup:
Priya: adding postmortem attendees: Maya, Jonah, Nadia, Liu, Evan, Priya, CS lead.
Nadia: note for postmortem: add root cause pointer to recent quantization change merged last week. We should require canary ramping for kernel-level changes.
Maya (on-call): agreed — add mandatory 24h canary + health gate for inline quant changes; add to deployment guide.
Jonah R.: final ask: implement a regional health composite monitor that includes routing metrics, backend healthy targets, and sustained error rate. I'll prototype in the alerting repo.
Maya (on-call): thanks all. I'm updating the incident doc with timeline, commands, and customer impact numbers now.
SRE-Bot: Incident channel archived, followups tracked in #postmortems and the incident doc.
